# Gcore Account settings

> Manage Gcore account settings including profile details, billing, users, access tokens, audit logs, and notifications.

- [Account settings](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings.md): Manage Gcore account settings including profile details, billing, users, access tokens, audit logs, and notifications.

## My profile
- [My profile settings](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/my-profile/overview.md): Manage Gcore profile settings, two-factor authentication, password changes, last logins, and login filters.
- [Set up two-factor authentication](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/my-profile/two-factor-authentication.md): Set up two-factor authentication (2FA) with an authenticator app, generate backup codes, and sign in securely.
- [Change or reset a password](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/my-profile/change-password.md): Change a Gcore account password from the profile settings or reset a forgotten password by email.
- [Missing password reset email](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/my-profile/password-reset-email.md): Troubleshoot a missing password reset email by checking spam, requesting a new reset, and contacting Gcore Support.

## Account
- [Account overview](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/account/overview.md): Manage Gcore account details, billing address, tax and currency settings, payment methods, services, and company account conversion.
- [Create an account for an individual or legal entity](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/account/create-account.md): Create a Gcore account as an individual or legal entity using email, Google, or GitHub, with contract options for businesses.
- [Create an additional account and switch between accounts](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/account/additional-accounts.md): Create an additional Gcore account and switch between accounts at sign-in when one login belongs to several accounts.
- [Disable or resume services](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/account/services.md): Disable or resume a Gcore service by contacting Gcore Support, noting that service data is deleted after the suspension period.
- [Account deletion](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/account/account-deletion.md): Requesting Gcore account deletion removes services and personal data, with a 10 day cancellation window and identity verification.

## Billing
- [Billing overview](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/billing/overview.md): Gcore billing overview explains monthly consumption data collection and Pay-As-You-Go threshold billing charged at 4 EUR or 4 USD.
- [Expenses](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/billing/expenses.md): Cloud project costs and reserved resource costs appear in Cost Report and Reservation Cost Report in Gcore Cloud Management.
- [Payments and payment methods](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/billing/payments.md): Manage Gcore payments and payment methods, including history, statuses, filters, saved cards, verification, removal, and balance top-ups.
- [Bonuses and discounts](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/billing/bonuses-and-discounts.md): View bonus credits, promo codes, and active discounts for a Gcore account, including bonus statuses, applicability, and debiting.
- [Trial conditions](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/billing/trial-conditions.md): Gcore trial conditions list which services offer free trials, duration and limits, and how to start a trial.
- [VAT rates in different countries for an individual and legal entity](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/billing/vat-rates.md): VAT rates for individuals and organizations by country, including EU reverse charge rules and 0% rates.
- [Tax location](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/billing/tax-location.md): Find how Gcore calculates tax location from billing address and VAT number, and what tax rate changes mean for invoices.
- [Data deletion](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/billing/data-deletion.md): Gcore data deletion timelines and retention periods by product after service suspension.

## Users
- [About users](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/users/about-users.md): Gcore user roles and rights explained, including Administrator, Engineer, and Purge and Prefetch permissions for account management.
- [Manage users](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/users/manage-users.md): Manage Gcore users by inviting, listing, updating roles and profiles, viewing account details, and deleting users.
- [API tokens](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/api-tokens.md): Create, manage, and delete Gcore access tokens with custom expiration, role assignments, and SSO support for automated processes.
- [Manage notification settings](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/notifications.md): Configure email notification settings for Gcore account users, including important, general, and product alerts.

## Support and resources
- [Technical support](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/how-quickly-our-support-team-will-respond-to-you.md): Gcore technical support response times depend on the support plan, request priority, and current team workload.
- [Be aware of the service status, scheduled and emergency maintenance](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/be-aware-of-the-service-status-scheduled-and-emergency-maintenance.md): Subscribe to Gcore Status Page updates by email, Slack, or webhook to track service status, outages, and scheduled maintenance.
- [Roadmap: submit feedback and track feature development](https://docs.gcore.com/account-settings/roadmap-provide-feedback-suggest-new-features-follow-development.md): Submit feature requests and track their development status on the Gcore Roadmap public feedback board, with product boards and a changelog.

# Gcore Developer Tools

> REST API, SDKs, MCP Server, Terraform.


## REST API
- [Gcore REST API](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/rest-api/overview.md): Gcore REST overview covers authentication, base URLs, and a step-by-step learning path for all Gcore products.
- [API basics](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/rest-api/api-basics.md): Gcore HTTP request basics cover choosing tools like curl, JSON responses, environment variables, and HTTP status codes.
- [Authenticate to the Gcore API](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/rest-api/authentication.md): Create a Gcore token, set it as an environment variable, and verify it to authenticate requests.
- [Make the first Gcore API call](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/rest-api/first-api-call.md): Set up a token, project ID, and region to make the first Gcore Cloud resource call.
- [Asynchronous operations and task polling](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/rest-api/async-operations.md): Gcore Cloud write operations return a task ID immediately. Poll the task until its state is FINISHED, then read created resource IDs.
- [Error handling](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/rest-api/error-handling.md): Gcore error handling explains response structure, common error types, status codes, and retry strategy for failed requests.
- [Pagination](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/rest-api/pagination.md): Gcore list endpoints return paginated results using limit and offset, with count and results fields to iterate through all pages.
- [API tools](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/rest-api/tools.md): Use Postman, HTTPie, and VS Code REST Client to call Gcore Cloud endpoints.

## SDKs
- [Gcore API SDKs](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/sdks/overview.md): Official Gcore SDKs for Python and Go, plus JavaScript fetch and axios options, with async task polling guidance.
- [Python SDK](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/sdks/python.md): Use the Gcore Python SDK to install, initialize clients, make calls, paginate, handle errors, retries, timeouts, and async requests.
- [Go SDK](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/sdks/go.md): Use the Gcore Go SDK to make typed REST calls, initialize the client, poll tasks, paginate results, and handle errors and retries.

## MCP Server
- [Gcore MCP Server overview](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/mcp-server/gcore-mcp-server-overview.md): Gcore MCP Server lets AI assistants manage Gcore services with natural language requests and supports setup, clients, and permissions.
- [Install and configure Gcore MCP Server](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/mcp-server/install-and-configure-gcore-mcp-server.md): Install and configure Gcore MCP Server with prerequisites, environment variables, and Cloud defaults for AI clients.
- [Connect Cursor IDE to Gcore MCP Server](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/mcp-server/connect-cursor-to-gcore-mcp-server.md): Connect Cursor IDE to Gcore MCP Server, configure tool patterns, verify the connection, and test queries.
- [Connect Claude Code to Gcore MCP Server](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/mcp-server/connect-claude-code-to-gcore-mcp-server.md): Set up Claude Code with Gcore MCP Server, authenticate, configure the server, and verify the connection.
- [Available products and tools](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/mcp-server/gcore-mcp-server-available-products-and-tools.md): Gcore MCP Server products and tools cover CDN, cloud, storage, networking, security, DNS, FastEdge, IAM, and streaming.
- [Filter tools with GCORE_TOOLS](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/mcp-server/filter-tools-with-gcore-tools.md): Control which tools the Gcore MCP Server exposes with the GCORE_TOOLS environment variable using toolsets, wildcards, and exact names.
- [Explore and debug tools with MCP Inspector](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/mcp-server/test-tools-with-mcp-inspector.md): Explore and debug Gcore MCP Server tools with MCP Inspector, connecting over stdio or HTTP to test tool schemas and execution errors.

## Terraform
- [Overview](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/terraform/overview.md): Gcore provider overview covers configuration and managing cloud and CDN resources with version-controlled infrastructure code.
- [Get started with Terraform](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/terraform/get-started-with-terraform.md): Set up Gcore infrastructure as code with the Gcore provider, from installation to applying configuration.
- [Manage a Terraform project](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/terraform/use-variables-and-organize-a-terraform-project.md): Manage an infrastructure as code project with input variables, sensitive values, and tfvars files for each deployment stage.
- [Import existing Gcore infrastructure into Terraform](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/terraform/import-existing-gcore-infrastructure-into-terraform.md): Bring existing Gcore resources under infrastructure as code management by importing them into state files with resource types and IDs.
- [Migrate from Gcore Terraform provider v0 to v2](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/terraform/migrate-v0-to-v2.md): Steps to migrate the Gcore provider from v0 to v2, covering resource renames, attribute changes, and manual re-import.
- [Copy resources across environments](https://docs.gcore.com/developer-tools/terraform/copy-resources-across-environments.md): Copy resources across environments using variables and workspaces to keep preproduction and production configurations identical.

# Gcore CDN

> Gcore CDN documentation covers setup, billing, resource configuration, caching, security, video delivery, and performance monitoring.

- [CDN](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn.md): Gcore CDN documentation covers setup, billing, resource configuration, caching, security, video delivery, and performance monitoring.

## Getting Started

## Create a CDN resource
- [CDN resource overview](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/create-a-cdn-resource/overview.md): Compare Standard CDN and Video Streaming resource types, their features, use cases, and limits for delivering domains through Gcore CDN.
- [Create a CDN resource](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/create-a-cdn-resource/create-a-cdn-resource.md): Create a Gcore CDN resource by setting up an origin group, adding a domain, and completing DNS with a CNAME record or delegated zone.
- [Create a CDN resource for video streaming](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/create-a-cdn-resource/create-a-cdn-resource-for-video-streaming.md): Set up a Gcore CDN resource for video streaming with HLS, MPEG-DASH, HTTP-FLV, or MP4 delivery, plus origin shielding and secure tokens.

## Integrate CDN with CMS and other platforms
- [CMS and platform integrations](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms.md): Guides for integrating Gcore CDN with content management systems, ecommerce platforms, forums, and cloud storage services.
- [Use an AWS S3 static website as a CDN origin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-aws-s3.md): Set up an AWS S3 static website as a Gcore CDN origin, configure a custom domain, and test content delivery.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with b2evolution](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-b2evolution.md): Configure a Gcore CDN custom domain for b2evolution static assets by editing the advanced configuration file.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Cloudflare](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-cloudflare.md): Set up a Gcore CDN resource with Cloudflare by adding a DNS only CNAME record and matching origin settings.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Concrete CMS](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-concrete5.md): Integrate a Gcore CDN resource with Concrete CMS using the Use CDN add-on to serve static assets through a custom domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Craft CMS](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-craft.md): Configure a Gcore CDN domain as the Craft CMS filesystem base URL so asset URLs resolve through the CDN.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with CS-Cart](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-cs-cart.md): Install the Universal CDN add-on in CS-Cart to rewrite image, CSS, and JavaScript URLs through a Gcore CDN domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Django CMS](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-django-cms.md): Configure Django CMS static and media URLs to serve assets through a Gcore CDN resource.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Drupal](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-drupal.md): Install and configure the Drupal CDN module to serve CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, and videos through a Gcore CDN custom domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Google Cloud Storage](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-google-cloud-storage.md): Set up a Gcore CDN resource with a Google Cloud Storage bucket origin for public asset delivery through a custom domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with IPB](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-ipb.md): Configure IP.Board 3.2 to 3.4 to serve images, CSS, and JavaScript from a Gcore CDN custom domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Invision Community Classic 4.x](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-ips.md): Configure Gcore CDN custom URLs for Invision Community Classic 4.x file storage and troubleshoot integration issues.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Joomla](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-joomla.md): Integrate a CDN resource with Joomla using the CDN for Joomla extension, covering setup, configuration, and troubleshooting.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Kirby](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-kirby.md): Integrate a Gcore CDN resource with Kirby by setting media and assets URLs to a custom domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Magento](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-magento.md): Configure Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce to serve static and media files through a Gcore CDN resource.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Perch](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-perch.md): Integrate a Gcore CDN resource with Perch by updating config files and bucket paths to serve resources from a custom domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with PrestaShop](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-prestashop.md): Configure a Gcore CDN resource as a PrestaShop media server to cache and deliver store images, theme files, and module assets.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with PyroCMS 2.x](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-pyrocms.md): Configure a Gcore CDN resource custom domain in PyroCMS 2.x admin integration settings to serve static assets.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with SocialEngine](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-socialengine.md): Configure a Gcore CDN resource with SocialEngine to cache and deliver static JavaScript and CSS files through a custom HTTPS domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with TYPO3](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-typo3.md): Configure TYPO3 Replacer extension rules to serve generated assets and public files through a Gcore CDN resource.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with vBulletin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-vbulletin.md): Set up a Gcore CDN resource for self-hosted vBulletin 6, with caching rules for static assets and no-cache rules for private content.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with Webasyst](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-webasyst.md): Connect a Gcore CDN resource to Webasyst by setting the CDN field to a custom domain and verifying asset URLs.

## Wordpress
- [Integrate a CDN resource with WordPress using the Gcore plugin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/wordpress/integrate-cdn-resource-with-wordpress-gcore-plugin.md): Integrate a Gcore CDN resource with WordPress using the Gcore plugin, including URL rewriting and troubleshooting.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with WordPress using WP Rocket](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/wordpress/integrate-cdn-resource-with-wordpress-rocket-plugin.md): Configure WP Rocket to rewrite WordPress static asset URLs to a Gcore CDN custom domain for faster edge delivery.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with WordPress using W3 Total Cache](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/wordpress/integrate-cdn-resource-with-wordpress-w3-total-cache-plugin.md): Set up W3 Total Cache Generic Mirror to serve WordPress static files from a Gcore CDN custom domain.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with WordPress using WP Super Cache](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/wordpress/integrate-cdn-resource-with-wordpress-wp-supercache-plugin.md): Configure a Gcore CDN resource with WordPress using the WP Super Cache plugin and its Simple CDN settings.
- [Integrate a CDN resource with X-Cart 4.4.x](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-x-cart.md): Set up a Gcore CDN custom domain for X-Cart 4.4.x by editing PHP and Smarty files to serve skin, image, and cache assets.
- [Integrate CDN resource with XenForo](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-cms/integrate-cdn-resource-with-xenforo.md): Configure XenForo externalDataUrl and javaScriptUrl to serve avatars, thumbnails, and JavaScript from a Gcore CDN custom domain.
- [Extend CDN functionality with FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-fastedge.md): Extend CDN functionality with FastEdge by attaching WebAssembly applications to request and response stages.

## Configure an origin
- [Allow Gcore CDN access to an origin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/configure-an-origin/add-cdn-servers-to-the-origin-acl-whitelist.md): Grant Gcore CDN edge servers access to a restricted origin using an HTTP auth header or public IP and network allowlists.
- [Configure HTTP/2 on the origin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/configure-an-origin/configure-http-2-on-the-origin.md): Configure HTTP2 on the origin server for Nginx and Apache to benefit clients connecting directly.
- [CDN timeouts](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/getting-started/cdn-timeouts.md): Gcore CDN timeout defaults for origin connections and client requests, including proxy read, connect, send, and keepalive values.
- [About CDN resources interface: how it is arranged](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/about-cdn-resources-interface-how-it-is-arranged.md): Overview of the Gcore CDN resources page covering creation, management, filtering, search, statuses, options, and deletion.
- [Origin groups for CDN resources](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/add-an-origin-group.md): Origin groups for CDN resources define multiple origins with load balancing, failover, and backup options for content delivery.

## CDN resource options

## General
- [Specify an origin and the origin pull protocol](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/general/specify-an-origin-and-the-origin-pull-protocol.md): Set the CDN origin pull protocol to HTTP, HTTPS, or both, and assign an origin group for content fetching.
- [Use a private bucket as an origin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/general/use-a-private-bucket-as-an-origin.md): Configure a private S3 bucket as a CDN origin with authentication, origin groups, and credential rotation.
- [Enable origin SSL validation](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/general/enable-origin-ssl-validation.md): Enable origin SSL validation for CDN by uploading a trusted CA certificate, retrieving its ID, and turning on validation for the resource.
- [Set a custom domain for CDN](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/general/create-and-set-a-custom-domain-for-the-content-delivery-via-cdn.md): Set a custom domain for CDN static content, check DNS status, add extra domains, and point CNAME records to Gcore.
- [Enable and configure origin shielding](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/general/enable-and-configure-origin-shielding.md): Enable origin shielding for a CDN resource and choose the shield location closest to the origin to reduce requests reaching it.
- [Suspend a CDN resource automatically or manually](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/general/suspend-a-cdn-resource-automatically-or-manually.md): Suspend a CDN resource automatically after 90 days of inactivity or manually, and enable or delete it when needed.
- [Customize connection and read timeouts](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/general/customize-connection-and-read-timeouts.md): Configure custom connection and read timeouts for Gcore CDN resources to control origin waits and avoid 504 Gateway Timeout errors.

## Cache
- [CDN cache lifetime configuration](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin.md): Configure CDN cache lifetime from origin headers or CDN settings, including custom expiry by response code and disabling caching.
- [Set up a CDN resource to follow origin redirects](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/set-up-a-cdn-resource-to-follow-origin-redirects.md): Configure a Gcore CDN resource to follow origin redirects and cache the target response for selected status codes.
- [Specify cache lifetime for user browsers](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-for-user-browsers.md): Control browser caching for CDN resources by choosing origin controlled or CDN controlled cache lifetime.
- [Ignore Set-Cookie or query string parameters when caching content on CDN servers](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers.md): Control how query string parameters and Set-Cookie headers affect CDN caching with ignore modes for cache keys.
- [Always online: serve stale cache when the origin cannot provide a fresh response](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/always-online-provide-the-stale-cache-if-the-origin-is-unavailable.md): Always Online serves stale cached content when the origin cannot provide a fresh response.
- [Cache Sharding: share cache between CDN servers](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/cache-sharding-share-cache-between-cdn-servers.md): Cache Sharding lets CDN servers in one PoP share cached content using consistent hashing to improve performance.
- [Modify cache key](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/modify-cache-key.md): Choose request variables that separate cached objects on a CDN resource and manage cache key modification settings.

## Access
- [Control access to the content with country, referrer, IP, and user agents policies](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/security/control-access-to-the-content-with-country-referrer-ip-and-user-agents-policies.md): Limit CDN resource requests with country, referrer, IP, and user agent access policies using allow or block by default modes.
- [Set up a redirect from HTTP to HTTPS](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/security/set-up-a-redirect-from-http-to-https.md): Redirect all HTTP requests for a CDN resource to HTTPS after enabling HTTPS and attaching an SSL certificate.

## Secure token
- [About secure token](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/security/use-a-secure-token/about-secure-token.md): Gcore CDN Secure Token protects files from unwanted downloads by making links temporary or restricting access by IP address.
- [Configure and use secure token](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/security/use-a-secure-token/configure-and-use-secure-token.md): Restrict CDN content access with a secure token using an MD5 hash and expiration timestamp, covering setup, signed URLs, and IP binding.
- [Specify HTTP methods allowed for content requests from the CDN](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/security/specify-http-methods-allowed-for-content-requests-from-the-cdn.md): Restrict which HTTP methods a CDN resource accepts for content requests, allowing GET and HEAD and blocking others with 405 responses.
- [Set the hostname passed in SNI requests to the origin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/security/set-the-hostname-passed-in-sni-requests-to-the-origin-server.md): Configure the SNI hostname CDN servers send to the origin, choosing dynamic or custom modes for HTTPS origin pulls.
- [Specify TLS versions allowed for content requests from the CDN](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/security/choose-tls-versions.md): Control which TLS protocol versions HTTPS clients can use for CDN content requests, with TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 recommended.

## Security
- [Protect CDN resources with Gcore WAAP](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cdn-security/protect-cdn-resources-with-waap.md): Enable Gcore WAAP for CDN resources to block malicious HTTP requests and create rules that turn protection off for specific URL paths.

## Compression
- [Configure Gzip and Brotli compression](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/compression/configure-gzip-and-brotli-compression.md): Enable Gzip and Brotli compression for Gcore CDN resources, including precedence, requirements, and disabling Gzip.
- [Configure fetch compression](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/compression/configure-fetch-compression.md): Enable Fetch compressed on a CDN resource so servers pull GZip content from the origin and serve it without decompressing.
- [Configuring HTTP status codes for CDN-hosted content](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/specify-custom-http-status-code-for-the-content-delivered-by-the-cdn.md): Set custom HTTP status codes for CDN-hosted content, with scheduling and rule-based delivery for specific paths.
- [Optimize large file delivery](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/optimize-large-file-delivery.md): Enable large file delivery optimization to cache CDN content in 10 MB chunks using HTTP range requests.
- [Rewrite: redirect requests from the CDN to the origin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/rewrite-redirect-requests-from-the-cdn-to-the-origin.md): Change CDN request paths before fetching from the origin with nginx rewrite rules and redirect flags.
- [Proxy WebSocket connections to the origin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/websockets-allow-permanent-connections-with-the-origin.md): Proxy WebSocket connections through Gcore CDN to the origin, with default settings for DNS delegation and CNAME resources.

## HTTP headers
- [Specify HTTP headers that CDN adds to requests to the origin](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/http-headers/specify-http-headers-that-cdn-adds-to-requests-to-the-origin.md): Configure request headers that Gcore CDN adds to origin requests, including header names, values, and limits.
- [Add the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header to the browser response](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/http-headers/add-the-access-control-allow-origin-header-to-the-browser-response.md): Configure CORS with the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header for Gcore CDN responses using resource settings, rules, or origin server.
- [Add or hide response headers](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/http-headers/add-or-hide-response-headers.md): Add or hide CDN response headers in Gcore, including multiple values and hiding selected or all headers.
- [Configure and check the host header](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/http-headers/configure-and-check-the-host-header.md): Set a custom or forwarded Host header for CDN origin requests and verify the origin accepts it.
- [Identify the client protocol with X-Forwarded-Proto](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/http-headers/use-the-x-forwarded-proto-header-to-identify-the-protocol-used-for-cdn-servers-requests.md): X-Forwarded-Proto shows whether a client used HTTP or HTTPS to reach a Gcore CDN edge server.
- [Network limits: set the content delivery speed to end users](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/network-limits-set-the-content-delivery-speed-to-end-users.md): Set a CDN download speed limit per connection with static or dynamic modes to control content delivery speed to end users.

## Image optimization (paid)
- [About Image Stack](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/image-optimization-paid/about-image-stack.md): Image Stack optimizes JPG and PNG images on the fly with quality, compression, resize, and crop operations on a CDN.
- [Enable Image Stack](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/image-optimization-paid/enable-image-stack.md): Enable Image Stack on a CDN resource or rule to optimize JPG and PNG images with quality, compression, resize, and crop settings.

## Image stack tools
- [Configure image compression to WebP and AVIF](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/image-optimization-paid/image-stack-tools/configure-image-compression-to-webp-and-avif.md): Convert JPG and PNG images to WebP or AVIF during CDN delivery to reduce file size without visible quality loss.
- [Change image quality](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/image-optimization-paid/image-stack-tools/change-image-quality.md): Reduce CDN image quality with Gcore Image Stack presets or URL query parameters for JPG and PNG delivery.
- [Crop images](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/image-optimization-paid/image-stack-tools/crop-images.md): Crop trims JPG or PNG images before CDN delivery using query parameters to set aspect ratio and crop location.
- [Reduce image size](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/image-optimization-paid/image-stack-tools/reduce-image-size.md): Reduce image size by adding Resize query parameters to image URLs, with Image Stack enabled on the CDN.
- [Possible Image Stack errors](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/image-optimization-paid/possible-image-stack-errors.md): Diagnose Image Stack errors that break images or return originals, including compression, quality, resize, and crop operation failures.
- [Query String Forwarding: forward parameters to sub-requests](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/query-string-forwarding.md): Query String Forwarding copies selected query parameters to nested HLS and MPEG-DASH manifests and segments on Gcore CDN.

## Rules for particular files
- [Create a rule manually or from a template to configure settings for particular files](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/rules-for-particular-files/create-a-rule-manually-or-from-a-template-to-configure-settings-for-particular-files.md): Create CDN rules manually or from a template to override caching and other settings for specific files by URI pattern or regex.
- [Create and use CDN rule templates](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/rules-for-particular-files/create-a-cdn-resource-rule-template-manually-or-use-a-system-one.md): Create custom and system CDN rule templates to preset file paths, origin pull protocols, and option overrides for rules.
- [Block crawling of a CDN domain](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/cdn-resource-options/rules-for-particular-files/set-robots-txt-to-avoid-adding-to-index-by-web-crawlers.md): Block web crawlers from crawling a CDN custom domain by returning a disallow robots.txt response.
- [CDN cache purging and purge history](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/clear-cdn-resource-cache-by-url-pattern-or-all.md): Clear CDN cache by URL, pattern, or all and review purge history for Gcore CDN resources.

## Grafana
- [View Edge Network statistics in Grafana](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/grafana/view-cdn-statistics-in-grafana.md): Grafana plugin for Gcore Edge Network statistics with CDN, DNS, FastEdge, and WAAP dashboards.
- [CDN billing](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/how-the-cdn-service-and-its-additional-options-are-billed.md): CDN billing covers monthly traffic and request limits, overage charges, payment history, service suspension, and changing plans.

## IP configuration options
- [Bring Your Own IP](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/ip-configuration-options/byoip.md): Bring Your Own IP lets Gcore announce customer-owned IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes for CDN resources, using either a Gcore ASN or a customer ASN.
- [Dedicated IP](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/ip-configuration-options/dedicated-ip.md): Request a dedicated Gcore CDN IP or subnet to give a resource exclusive addresses and reduce shared IP reputation risks.
- [CDN content prefetching](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/load-the-content-to-cdn-before-users-request-it.md): CDN content prefetching loads files into cache before visitor requests, with limits and verification steps.

## Logs

- [Raw Logs export](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/logs/raw-logs-export-cdn-resource-logs-to-your-storage.md): Raw Logs exports CDN request logs hourly to S3, FTP, or SFTP storage with statuses, intervals, and log fields.
- [CDN resource logs in Log viewer](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/logs/log-viewer-view-and-download-cdn-resource-logs.md): View and download CDN resource logs in Log viewer, filter requests by CNAME, IP, status, and export CSV or TSV.

## Troubleshooting
- [Common setup issues](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/common-setup-issues.md): Fix common CDN setup issues like 503 errors, redirect loops, host header problems, file downloads, and SSL certificate errors.
- [Gcore CDN error status codes](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/gcore-error-status-codes.md): Gcore CDN error status codes explained, including 403, 404, 410, and other HTTP errors with causes and fixes.
- [Traceparent header for troubleshooting](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/traceparent-header-for-troubleshooting.md): Use the Gcore CDN traceparent header to identify requests and correlate trace IDs in raw.
- [Unavailable content after CDN resource creation](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/content-is-unavailable-after-a-cdn-resource-creation-how-to-solve-the-issue.md): Fix unavailable CDN content after resource creation by checking origin response, host header, DNS, SSL, and cache settings.
- [Low cache hit ratio troubleshooting](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/cache-percentage-is-low-how-to-solve-the-issue.md): Troubleshoot a low CDN cache hit ratio by checking caching headers, traffic patterns, and common causes of origin fetches.
- [Slow content delivery troubleshooting](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/content-delivery-speed-is-low-how-to-solve-the-issue.md): Troubleshoot slow CDN content delivery by comparing origin and edge speeds, checking cache hit ratio, and reviewing large file settings.
- [An SSL certificate isn't working: how to solve the issue](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/an-ssl-certificate-isn-t-working-how-to-solve-to-issue.md): Troubleshoot SSL certificate errors including attachment failures, Let's Encrypt issuance problems, and TLS handshake issues.
- [CDN 3xx response troubleshooting](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/3xx-error-how-to-solve-cdn-issues-with-redirect.md): Troubleshoot CDN 301 and 302 redirects by checking CDN settings, origin pull, Host header, and SNI before comparing response codes.
- [CDN 4xx response troubleshooting](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/4xx-error-how-to-solve-cdn-issues-with-the-limited-access-and-content-non-existence.md): Troubleshoot CDN 4xx responses by checking status causes, origin content availability, resource settings, and response logs.
- [CDN 5xx response troubleshooting](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/troubleshooting/5xx-error-how-to-solve-server-issues.md): Troubleshoot CDN 5xx response errors by checking origin availability, CDN resource settings, pull protocol, Host header, and logs.

## Video CDN
- [Video CDN Overview](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/video-cdn-overview.md): Video CDN overview covers Gcore CDN video delivery, supported formats like HLS and DASH, low latency, security, and setup requirements.
- [Common Media Client Data (CMCD)](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/cmcd.md): Send Common Media Client Data (CMCD) v1 from video players to Gcore CDN for playback context in delivery logs.
- [HLS and LL-HLS via CDN](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/hls.md): Deliver HLS and low-latency HLS streams through Gcore CDN with cache rules, supported formats, and setup requirements.
- [Improve video delivery speed for low-traffic accounts](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/improve-video-delivery-speed.md): Speed up video delivery for low-traffic accounts by warming the CDN cache, prefetching popular content, and tuning cache TTL settings.
- [DASH and LL-DASH via CDN](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/dash.md): Deliver MPEG-DASH and low-latency LL-DASH live streams through Gcore CDN with Chunked-Proxy for 2 to 4 second latency.
- [Multi-codec VOD delivery over CDN](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/multi-codec-vod-delivery.md): Deliver HEVC, AV1, VP9, and H.264 VOD renditions over Gcore CDN to cut bandwidth while keeping H.264 fallback for older devices.
- [Origin shielding for video delivery](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/origin-shielding-for-video.md): Origin shielding for video delivery reduces origin requests for live events and VOD libraries by caching at a shield location.
- [Secure Token for Video CDN](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/secure-token.md): Secure Token for Video CDN protects HLS and MPEG-DASH streams with Query String Forwarding for manifests and segments.
- [Auto-refresh CDN secure tokens](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/secure-token-auto-refresh.md): Set short-lived CDN secure tokens to expire in 60 seconds and refresh them automatically in the player to stop link sharing.
- [Troubleshoot video delivery](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/troubleshoot-video-delivery.md): Diagnose video delivery issues such as 403 and 410 errors, buffering, 504 timeouts, live MPEG-DASH 404s, and CDN caching problems.
- [HTTP-FLV Live and VOD Delivery](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/video-cdn/flv-streaming.md): Configure HTTP-FLV live and VOD delivery on Gcore CDN with low-latency streaming, authentication, origin failover, and monitoring.
- [CDN reports and overview](https://docs.gcore.com/cdn/view-statistics-of-a-cdn-resource.md): Track CDN performance, traffic, cache, errors, and security with Overview dashboards and statistics reports for Gcore CDN resources.

# Gcore FastEdge

> FastEdge is a serverless edge compute platform for running WebAssembly applications on Gcore's global edge network.

- [FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge.md): FastEdge is a serverless edge compute platform for running WebAssembly applications on Gcore's global edge network.

## Get started
- [FastEdge overview](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started.md): FastEdge runs WebAssembly apps on Gcore's global edge network for personalization, authentication, and image processing.
- [Set up Rust for FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/setup-rust-modern.md): Set up Rust for FastEdge using the Modern Rust SDK, WASI-HTTP, wstd crate, and wasm32-wasip2 target to build a cdylib WebAssembly library.
- [Set up Rust for FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/setup-rust-legacy.md): Set up the Legacy Rust SDK for FastEdge by adding the wasm32-wasip1 target, configuring a Cargo project, and verifying the toolchain.
- [Set up JavaScript for FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/setup-javascript.md): Set up the FastEdge JavaScript SDK to compile a fetch handler into a WebAssembly binary for edge deployment.
- [Set up Rust for FastEdge CDN apps](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/setup-rust-cdn.md): Set up Rust for FastEdge CDN apps by adding the wasm32-wasip1 target, configuring a Cargo project, and verifying the toolchain.

## Applications

## HTTP Applications
- [Create FastEdge HTTP applications](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/create-fastedge-apps.md): Build, deploy, and test FastEdge HTTP applications from a WebAssembly binary or template on the Gcore edge network.
- [Render Markdown at the edge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/render-markdown.md): Deploy the FastEdge Markdown renderer to turn Markdown files into HTML pages at the edge using a configurable root URL.
- [Redirect visitors by location](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/geolocation-redirect.md): Set up a FastEdge geolocation redirect to send visitors to country-specific URLs using environment variables and Geo-IP data.
- [Build a FastEdge HTTP application](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/get-started-http.md): Build and deploy a FastEdge HTTP application from a WebAssembly handler written in Rust or JavaScript.
- [Call an external API from a FastEdge app](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/call-external-api-rust.md): Build a FastEdge app in Rust that makes outbound HTTP calls from the handler and returns parsed JSON.

## CDN Applications
- [Extend CDN functionality with FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/integrate-cdn-with-fastedge.md): Extend CDN functionality with FastEdge by attaching WebAssembly applications to request and response stages.
- [Build and deploy a FastEdge CDN application](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/get-started-cdn.md): Build and deploy a FastEdge CDN application by writing a handler, compiling it to WebAssembly, and uploading the binary.
- [Request and response properties](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/getting-started/cdn-properties.md): FastEdge CDN request and response properties can be read or modified with get_property and set_property host functions.
- [FastEdge application management](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/manage-apps.md): Manage FastEdge applications with metrics, logs, response headers, environment variables, secrets, and Edge Storage settings.
- [Create and manage templates](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/create-manage-templates.md): Create and manage FastEdge templates that package a WebAssembly binary with configuration for repeatable app deployment.

## Local development
- [Local development for FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/local-development/overview.md): Compare local development tools for FastEdge, including AI-assisted coding, a VS Code extension, and a headless test framework.
- [AI-assisted development for FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/local-development/ai-assisted-development.md): Use AI coding assistants to scaffold, build, and deploy FastEdge WebAssembly apps with the gcore-fastedge plugin and MCP server.
- [FastEdge extension for VS Code](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/local-development/vscode-extension.md): FastEdge extension for VS Code builds Rust, JavaScript, or AssemblyScript into Wasm and debugs FastEdge apps locally.
- [Test framework for FastEdge](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/local-development/test-framework.md): Test FastEdge Wasm binaries in Node.js with a headless suite, assertion helpers, a visual debugger, and Vitest or Jest integration.

## Secrets Manager
- [Secrets Manager](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/secrets-manager/manage-secrets.md): Secrets Manager stores encrypted values for FastEdge applications, with steps to create, edit, delete, and link secrets.
- [Secret rotation with slots](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/secrets-manager/slots.md): Secret rotation with slots stores multiple encrypted password versions and selects the right slot by index or Unix timestamp.

## Edge Storage
- [How it works](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/kv-stores/how-it-works.md): Edge Storage for FastEdge is a globally replicated key-value store with local replicas at every edge location, compared with Cache.
- [Edge Storage](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/kv-stores/manage-kv-store.md): Create and manage Edge Storage key-value stores for FastEdge applications, including adding pairs, uploading files, and setting expiration.
- [BYOD, Bring Your Own Database](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/kv-stores/byod.md): BYOD connects FastEdge Edge Storage to an external Redis-compatible database so applications use existing data without migration.
- [Sorted Set](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/kv-stores/sorted-set.md): Manage Gcore Edge Storage sorted sets by creating, editing, and deleting members with numeric scores.
- [Bloom Filter](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/kv-stores/bloom-filter.md): Create, edit, and delete Bloom Filters in Gcore Edge Storage for fast membership checks on large datasets.
- [Cache](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/cache.md): FastEdge Cache is a fast key-value store for transient request-time state, atomic counters, and rate limiting at each POP.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/troubleshooting.md): Fix FastEdge application failures with 5xx error codes, debug logging, missing headers, and common runtime issues.
- [FastEdge CLI](https://docs.gcore.com/fastedge/fastedge-cli.md): Run compiled FastEdge Wasm binaries locally over HTTP with fastedge-run to test edge applications without deploying.

# Gcore Edge Cloud

> Gcore Cloud offers on-demand IaaS and PaaS with compute, storage, networking, containers, databases, and observability across 30+ regions.

- [Cloud](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud.md): Gcore Cloud offers on-demand IaaS and PaaS with compute, storage, networking, containers, databases, and observability across 30+ regions.
- [Bandwidth and traffic](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bandwidth-and-traffic.md): Bandwidth limits and traffic billing for Gcore compute resources, including VMs and Bare Metal servers.
- [Billing](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/billing.md): Gcore Edge Cloud uses pay-as-you-go billing with per-minute charges, a 4 EUR or USD threshold, and suspension if payment fails.
- [Tags](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/tags.md): Tags are key-value pairs for organizing and identifying Gcore Cloud resources, with rules, filtering, and cost report usage.

## Getting started
- [Manage resource quotas](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/request-a-quota-increase.md): Check Gcore Cloud account quotas by region and request resource limit increases for compute, storage, network, and other services.

- [Cost reports](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/view-statistics-on-expenses.md): View Cloud cost reports and reservation cost reports to track resource usage, commitments, and export cost data.

## Virtual Machines

## Placement groups

## Bare Metal servers
- [About Bare Metal](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/about-bare-metal-servers.md): Gcore Bare Metal is a cloud service offering dedicated physical servers with full isolation and high performance.
- [Types of Bare Metal servers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/types-of-bare-metal-servers.md): Compare Gcore Bare Metal server types for high frequency, infrastructure, and storage workloads.
- [Create a Bare Metal server](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/create-a-bare-metal-server.md): Create a Gcore Bare Metal server by selecting a region, image, server type, and network interfaces, then requesting a quota increase.
- [Manage a Bare Metal server](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/manage-a-bare-metal-server.md): Manage a Bare Metal server with console access, power controls, network interfaces, tags, rebuild, rename, and delete operations.
- [Connect to Bare Metal via SSH](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/connect-to-your-bare-metal-server-via-ssh.md): Connect to a Linux Bare Metal server via SSH using key pairs or a password, with steps for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- [Bare Metal egress traffic](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/egress-traffic.md): Bare Metal egress traffic is billed per GB over the public network interface, while private network traffic stays free.

## Troubleshooting
- [Troubleshoot issues with an SSH connection](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-issues-with-ssh-connection.md): Fix SSH connection failures on Gcore virtual machines and bare metal servers, including key, username, public IP, and firewall problems.

## Advanced DDoS protection
- [About advanced DDoS protection for Bare Metal](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/advanced-ddos-protection/about-advanced-ddos-protection-for-bare-metal-servers.md): Advanced DDoS Protection for Bare Metal filters attack traffic through TMS, keeps servers online, and offers always-on mitigation.
- [Activate advanced DDoS protection for Bare Metal](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/advanced-ddos-protection/activate-advanced-ddos-protection-for-bare-metal-servers.md): Activate Advanced DDoS Protection for Bare Metal servers during creation or on existing public interfaces and manage profiles.

## Images
- [About images](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/images/about-images.md): An image is a copy of a disk file system used to create a virtual machine boot volume or distribute software.
- [Upload a custom image](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/images/upload-an-image-to-the-storage.md): Upload a custom image to Gcore from a public URL after checking supported formats, drivers, packages, and start modes.
- [Manage custom images](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/images/manage-custom-images.md): Manage Gcore Cloud custom images by viewing, renaming, tagging, deleting, and creating virtual instances from them.

## Networking
- [Create and manage a network](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/create-and-manage-a-network.md): Create and manage Gcore Cloud networks, attach or detach network interfaces to VMs, Bare Metal, Load Balancers, and Kubernetes clusters.
- [Create and manage a subnet](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/create-and-manage-a-subnetwork.md): Create and manage a subnet in a Gcore cloud network, including CIDR, DHCP, DNS, router settings, renaming, and deletion.
- [Create and manage a router](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/create-and-manage-a-router.md): Create and manage a Cloud Router in Gcore, attach subnets, configure static routes, and control traffic between networks.

## IP address
- [Create and configure a floating IP address](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/create-and-configure-a-floating-ip-address.md): Create, configure, reserve, assign, detach, and delete a floating IP address for Gcore Virtual Machines and Bare Metal servers.
- [Create and configure a reserved IP address](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/create-and-configure-a-reserved-ip-address.md): Create, assign, detach, and delete Gcore reserved IP addresses for virtual machines, bare metal servers, and load balancers.
- [Create and configure a virtual IP address](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/create-and-configure-a-virtual-ip-vip-address.md): Create and configure a virtual IP address (VIP) in Gcore Cloud for failover with Keepalived or as a secondary address.
- [Difference between virtual, floating, and reserved IP addresses](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/difference-between-virtual-floating-and-reserved-ip-addresses.md): Compare virtual, floating, and reserved IP addresses in Gcore Cloud, including use cases, assignment, failover, and billing.
- [Configure an allowed address pair](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/configure-an-allowed-address-pair.md): Configure allowed address pairs on a private network port to permit extra IP or CIDR addresses for a virtual machine.

## Load balancers
- [Create and configure a load balancer](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/create-and-configure-a-load-balancer.md): Create and configure a Gcore load balancer with region, flavor, network, listeners, pool, health check, timeouts, logging, and tags.
- [Add TLS certificates to a load balancer](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/add-certificates-to-load-balancer.md): Add TLS certificates to a load balancer listener using SNI and Secrets Manager for multiple secure domains.
- [Configure mutual TLS authentication](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/configure-mtls-authentication.md): Configure mutual TLS authentication for Gcore Load Balancers with server and CA certificates, TLS termination, and backend mTLS.
- [Manage load balancers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/manage-load-balancers.md): Manage Gcore load balancers, including statuses, settings, listeners, monitoring, logging, tags, DDoS protection, limits, and failover.
- [Logging for load balancers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/logging-for-load-balancers.md): Enable load balancer logging to send access logs to Gcore Logging, configure namespaces, topics, and destination regions.
- [Use annotations for load balancers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/use-annotations-for-load-balancers.md): Configure Gcore Load Balancers in Managed Kubernetes with annotations for type, flavor, IP, listeners, pools, logging, and DDoS protection.
- [Monitoring for load balancers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/monitoring-for-load-balancers.md): Monitor load balancers with a Prometheus metrics listener and Managed Logging that sends access logs to OpenSearch.
- [Add and configure a security group](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/add-and-configure-a-firewall.md): Create and manage security groups for Virtual Machines, including rules, tags, default groups, and Bare Metal servers.
- [Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP)](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/byoip.md): Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) lets organizations use their own public IP ranges with Gcore while preserving IP reputation and allowlists.
- [Cloud egress IP addresses](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/cloud-egress-ip-addresses.md): Find Gcore Cloud egress IP addresses and ranges to allowlist outbound traffic and automate allowlist updates.

## File shares
- [About file shares](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/file-shares/about-file-shares.md): Gcore File Shares provides NFS file storage for sharing data across Virtual Machines, Bare Metal servers, and Kubernetes pods.

- [Migrate data from S3 and EFS to Gcore](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/file-shares/how-to-migrate-data-from-s3.md): Move data from Amazon S3 or EFS to Gcore Object Storage or File Shares using rclone for cloud storage migration.

## Autoscaling
- [About autoscaling](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/autoscaling/about-autoscaling.md): Autoscaling adjusts node count in a Managed Kubernetes pool based on load, keeping it between the minimum and maximum.

- [Advanced cluster autoscaler settings](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/autoscaling/advanced-cluster-autoscaler-settings.md): Configure advanced cluster autoscaler settings, including cluster expander and parameters for scan interval and scale-down decisions.

- [Add users with limited rights to a Kubernetes cluster](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/add-users-with-limited-rights-to-a-kubernetes-cluster.md): Create a namespace-scoped ServiceAccount and kubeconfig to give limited Kubernetes cluster access without admin credentials.
- [Monitor load on a specific node](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/monitor-load-on-a-specific-node.md): View CPU, RAM, network traffic, and packet metrics for a Kubernetes worker node in Gcore Managed Kubernetes.

# Gcore AI

> Gcore AI documentation covers Everywhere Inference for edge model deployment and GPU Cloud for accelerated training and fine-tuning.

# Gcore Gclaw

> Gclaw is a fully managed OpenClaw AI agent with built-in inference on Gcore GPU infrastructure, chat access, and messaging integrations.

- [Gclaw](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw.md): Gclaw is a fully managed OpenClaw AI agent with built-in inference on Gcore GPU infrastructure, chat access, and messaging integrations.
- [Getting started](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/getting-started.md): Create and launch a Gclaw instance in about a minute, then use the chat interface to talk with the AI assistant.
- [Manage instance](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/manage-instance.md): Manage Gclaw instance settings with backup, restore, restart, and recreate options while understanding data persistence and recovery.
- [Configure API keys](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/api-keys.md): Configure external keys for Gclaw skills and see which credentials each skill requires.

## Integrations
- [Connect Telegram](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/connect-telegram.md): Connect Telegram to the Gclaw AI assistant by creating a bot, adding its token, and approving pairing.
- [Connect Discord](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/connect-discord.md): Connect Discord to the Gclaw AI assistant by creating a bot, adding its token, and inviting it to a server.
- [Security model](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/security.md): Gcore Gclaw security model explains shared responsibility for isolated virtual machines and OpenClaw agent privileges.
- [Limits and quotas](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/limits.md): Gclaw limits and quotas cover model context and output token limits, rate limits, and beta instance limits.
- [Pricing](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/pricing.md): Gclaw pricing covers Lite plan costs, token rates, a 7-day trial, beta limits, and third-party product terms.
- [SSH access to the Gclaw VM](https://docs.gcore.com/gclaw/ssh-access.md): Set up SSH access to the Gclaw VM by generating a key pair, authorizing the public key, finding the IP address, and connecting securely.
---

# Gcore Managed DNS

> Gcore Managed DNS is an authoritative DNS service with Anycast routing, dynamic responses, healthchecks, DNSSEC, and CDN integration.

- [Overview](https://docs.gcore.com/dns.md): Gcore Managed DNS is an authoritative DNS service with Anycast routing, dynamic responses, healthchecks, DNSSEC, and CDN integration.
- [Gcore Managed DNS glossary](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/gcore-dns-glossary.md): Definitions of key Gcore Managed DNS terms, including A record, AAAA record, CNAME, DNS zone, DNS query, and DNSSEC.
- [Getting started with Managed DNS](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/manage-a-dns-zone.md): Create and manage a Managed DNS zone, delegate nameservers, edit settings, import records, and delete zones in Gcore.
- [Migrate DNS from Cloudflare to Gcore](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/migrate-from-cloudflare.md): Move DNS from Cloudflare to Gcore by exporting the zone file, importing records, and switching nameservers at the registrar.

## Records
- [Supported DNS record types](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records.md): Gcore Managed DNS supports eleven DNS record types including A, AAAA, NS, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, CAA, HTTPS, SVCB, and PTR.
- [Manage DNS records](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/manage-dns-records-non-advanced-interface-mode.md): Create and manage DNS records in Gcore using the non-advanced interface mode, including record types, values, updates, and imports.
- [Manage DNS records (advanced interface mode with dynamic response)](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/manage-dns-records-advanced-interface-mode-with-balancing.md): Manage DNS records with dynamic response in Gcore Managed DNS advanced interface mode.
- [Import and export records](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/import-and-export-records.md): Export DNS zone records to a BIND zone file for backup or migration, and import records from a BIND file into an existing zone.
- [Create records in zone apex (CNAME flattening)](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/specify-cname-at-root.md): CNAME flattening lets Gcore Managed DNS create a CNAME at the zone apex by resolving it to A or AAAA records.
- [Configure DNS records for email](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/set-up-dns-for-sending-email.md): Set up A, MX, PTR, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC DNS records to route and authenticate email for a domain.
- [Setting up a PTR record and reverse DNS zone](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/set-up-a-ptr-record-and-reverse-dns-zone.md): Set up PTR records and reverse DNS zones for IPv4 and IPv6, including creation, verification, updates, and deletion.
- [Configure HTTPS records](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/what-is-an-https-record-and-how-is-it-configured.md): Configure HTTPS DNS records in Gcore Managed DNS to reduce connection round trips and manage record creation, updates, and deletion.

## Advanced managing
- [Dynamic response](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/configure-weight-balancing-and-geobalancing.md): Configure dynamic DNS responses with weighted shuffle, geo DNS, and geo distance pickers to control which records answer a query.
- [DNS Healthchecks](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-failover/configure-and-use-dns-failover.md): DNS Healthchecks monitor server availability and remove non-working IPs from DNS responses to keep sites online during outages.
- [Configure CDN integration](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-records/advanced-managing/cdn-integration.md): Configure CDN integration to link A or AAAA DNS records to a Gcore CDN resource, enabling direct resolution to CDN addresses.
- [Getting started with DNSSEC](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/getting-started-with-dnssec.md): Enable DNSSEC for a DNS zone, add the DS record at the registrar, and track the status lifecycle until active.

## Integrations
- [Configure OctoDNS with Gcore Managed DNS](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-plugins/use-gcore-dns-as-a-secondary-dns-with-octodns.md): Set up OctoDNS to sync DNS records from a primary provider to Gcore Managed DNS as a secondary DNS.
- [Get a Let's Encrypt certificate with Certbot](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-plugins/get-a-let-s-encrypt-certificate-with-certbot.md): Use the certbot-dns-gcore plugin to obtain and renew Let's Encrypt certificates with Gcore DNS validation.
- [Manage DNS zones and records via Terraform v0](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/dns-plugins/manage-dns-with-terraform.md): Manage DNS zones and records with Gcore provider v0, covering SOA, DNSSEC, A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, CAA, geo-balancing, and failover.
---

# Gcore Public DNS

> Gcore Public DNS is a free recursive resolver with IPv4 and IPv6 addresses supporting plain DNS, DoH, and DoT queries.

- [Public DNS](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/public-dns.md): Gcore Public DNS is a free recursive resolver with IPv4 and IPv6 addresses supporting plain DNS, DoH, and DoT queries.
- [Configure a DNS resolver](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/configure-plain-dns.md): Set up a plain DNS resolver with Gcore Public DNS addresses on Windows and macOS network settings.
- [Configure DNS over HTTPS and DNS over TLS](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/configure-doh-and-dot.md): Set up DNS over HTTPS and DNS over TLS with Gcore Public DNS using the DoH URL and DoT hostname gcoredns.com.
- [Troubleshoot Gcore Public DNS](https://docs.gcore.com/dns/troubleshoot-public-dns.md): Fix Gcore Public DNS issues caused by DHCP, VPN, browser DoH, blocked encrypted DNS ports, and Windows DoH provider registration.
---

# Gcore Hosting

> Gcore Hosting provides virtual and dedicated servers, DDoS protection, DNS hosting, payments, and technical support.

- [Hosting](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting.md): Gcore Hosting provides virtual and dedicated servers, DDoS protection, DNS hosting, payments, and technical support.

## Dedicated servers
- [Overview](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/about-dedicated-servers.md): Gcore Dedicated Servers offer exclusive physical machine resources with Intel Xeon processors in data centers worldwide.

## Before purchase
- [Test network connectivity before buying a server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/before-purchase/test-the-connectivity-between-your-location-and-the-server-you-want-to-buy.md): Check network connectivity, latency, BGP routing, and traceroute hops from Gcore locations to any IP address before buying a server.
- [Order a dedicated server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/order-a-dedicated-server.md): Order a dedicated server by selecting a data center and configuration, setting order parameters, and completing payment.
- [Upgrade your dedicated server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/upgrade-your-dedicated-server.md): Upgrade dedicated server hardware specifications and change the internet plan with support assistance and billing details.

## Manage
- [Access DCImanager](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/log-in-to-dcimanager.md): Access DCImanager to manage dedicated server hardware, restart or power off servers, and troubleshoot login errors.
- [Log in to IPMI](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/log-in-to-ipmi.md): Log in to IPMI for Gcore dedicated servers to monitor hardware, control power, and reinstall the operating system.

## Connect
- [Connect to a Windows server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/connect/connect-to-a-windows-server.md): Connect to a Windows server over RDP using Remote Desktop and credentials from the hosting panel or activation email.
- [Connect to a Linux server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/connect/connect-to-a-linux-server.md): Connect to a Linux server over SSH with credentials from the hosting dashboard or activation email.
- [Manage SSH keys](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/connect/linux-server/manage-ssh-keys.md): Set up SSH key authentication for Linux virtual servers, connect with a key pair, and remove a public key to revoke access.
- [Change the port for SSH connections](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/connect/linux-server/change-the-port-for-ssh-connections.md): Change the default SSH port from 22 to a custom number and update firewall rules to allow the new connection.

## Operating system
- [Install a Linux OS from your ISO image](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/operating-system/install-a-linux-os-from-your-iso-image.md): Install a Linux OS on a dedicated server by uploading an ISO image to DCImanager and booting the server from it.
- [Install a Linux OS from a template](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/operating-system/install-a-linux-os-from-a-template.md): Install a Linux OS from a template on a dedicated server using DCImanager, with supported distributions and custom setup options.

## Networking

## Additional IP addresses
- [Buy an additional IP address](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/networking/additional-ip-addresses/buy-an-additional-ip-address.md): Order additional IPv4 and IPv6 addresses for dedicated servers and virtual private servers, with limits and transfer options.
- [Configure an additional IP address](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/networking/additional-ip-addresses/configure-an-additional-ip-address.md): Configure an additional IP address in the operating system after purchase, including network interface settings and verification.
- [Connect dedicated servers into a VLAN](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/networking/connect-dedicated-servers-into-a-vlan.md): Connect dedicated servers into a VLAN by assigning the same VLAN to a switch port on each server.
- [Configure a 10 Gbps network card](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/networking/configure-a-10-gbps-network-card.md): Configure a 10 Gbps network card on a Gcore dedicated server by identifying and enabling the correct interface.
- [Set up a PTR record](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/set-up-a-ptr-record.md): Create a PTR record to map an IP address to a domain name for outbound email server deliverability.
- [Reboot a server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/manage/reboot-a-server.md): Reboot or restart a dedicated server from the Gcore server list or DCImanager using the context menu.
- [Dedicated server statistics](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/check-statistics-of-your-dedicated-server.md): View daily incoming and outgoing traffic and monthly overage against the included quota for Gcore dedicated servers.
- [Delete a dedicated server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/delete-a-dedicated-server.md): Deleting a dedicated server permanently removes it, erases all data, and stops billing charges.

## Troubleshooting
- [Server suspended for non-payment](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-a-server-that-was-suspended-for-non-payment.md): Fix a virtual server suspended for non-payment by recharging the account balance or using auto payment to reactivate it.
- [Server not responding to ping requests](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-a-server-that-is-not-responding-to-ping-requests.md): Troubleshoot a server that does not respond to ping requests, including primary and additional IP addresses and China connectivity blocks.
- [IP address is in blocklists](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/troubleshooting/remove-your-ip-address-from-blacklists.md): Check if an IP address is on email blocklists and follow removal instructions to improve email delivery.
- [Troubleshoot errors with ISO image installation](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-errors-with-iso-image-installation.md): Fix ISO image upload and mounting errors in DCI manager by checking file format, size limits, and IPMI proxy attachment.
- [Troubleshoot IPMI errors](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-ipmi-errors.md): Resolve common IPMI connection errors, login failures, and remote console issues in DCImanager.
- [Incorrect IP location](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-issues-with-an-incorrect-ip-location.md): Check an IP address location against MaxMind GeoIP and RIPEstat, and request a correction from Gcore support if the data is wrong.
- [Troubleshoot issues with SSH connection](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-issues-with-ssh-connection.md): Fix SSH connection failures by checking port 22, verifying credentials, and accessing the OS directly.
- [Troubleshoot packet loss and high ping](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/dedicated-servers/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-packet-loss-or-high-ping.md): Steps to diagnose packet loss and high ping between client and server, including VPN checks and support details.

## Virtual servers
- [About Virtual Servers](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/about-virtual-servers.md): Virtual Servers use KVM virtualization with dedicated RAM, disk, and vCPU, offered in KVM-SSD and KVM-HIGHCPU-SSD plans.

## Before purchase
- [Choose a virtual server for your needs](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/before-purchase/choose-a-virtual-server-for-your-needs.md): Compare Gcore virtual server plans, including KVM-SSD and KVM-HIGHCPU-SSD, to select the right configuration for specific workloads.
- [Test network connectivity before buying a server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/before-purchase/test-the-connectivity-between-your-location-and-the-server-you-want-to-buy.md): Check network connectivity, latency, BGP routing, and traceroute hops from Gcore locations to any IP address before buying a server.
- [Order a virtual server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/order-a-virtual-server.md): Order a Gcore virtual server, review server statuses, and manage renewal after selecting a plan and completing payment.
- [Upgrade your virtual server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/upgrade-your-virtual-server.md): Request a virtual server plan upgrade through Gcore support, with data and IP preserved and 30 to 60 minutes of downtime.

## Manage
- [Features and functions of VMmanager 6](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/main-features-and-functions-of-vmmanager-6.md): VMmanager 6 is a control panel for managing virtual private servers, covering interface sections, server actions, and panel specifics.

## Linux server

- [Connect to a Linux server via SSH](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/connect/linux-server/connect-to-linux-server-via-ssh.md): Connect to a Linux virtual server over SSH using the IP address, username, and password from the hosting instructions page.

## Operating system
- [Order a Windows Server](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/operating-system/buy-a-windows-server.md): Order Windows Server on KVM-SSD-4 or higher plans, with license fee and OS selection at checkout.
- [Install an OS from a template](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/operating-system/install-a-linux-os-from-a-template.md): Reinstall a virtual server operating system from predefined templates or a custom ISO, noting that all disk data is erased.
- [Install an OS from an ISO image](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/operating-system/install-a-linux-os-from-your-iso-image.md): Install an operating system from a custom ISO image in VMmanager by mounting a public URL as a bootable disk and rebooting the server.
- [Install an operating system from a template in VMmanager 6](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/operating-system/install-an-os-from-a-template-in-vmmanager-6.md): Reinstall an operating system from a template in VMmanager 6, choosing a distribution and version, with optional post-install scripts.
- [Install an OS from an ISO image in VMmanager 6](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/virtual-servers/manage/operating-system/install-an-os-from-iso-in-vmmanager-6.md): Mount an ISO image in VMmanager 6 to install an operating system, then connect via VNC and disconnect the image after setup.

## Payments
- [Pay for Gcore services](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/payments/pay-for-gcore-services-payment-methods.md): Pay for Gcore services by adding funds via PayPal, bank transfer, bank card, or Alipay, with currency set by the account provider.

- [Set up auto payment](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/payments/set-up-auto-payment.md): Set up auto payment to recharge account balance automatically for service renewals with a linked payment method and monthly limit.
- [Troubleshoot payment errors](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/payments/troubleshoot-payment-errors.md): Fix failed payments for PayPal, bank cards, AMEX, and AliPay, including insufficient funds, security declines, and Adyen errors.
- [Check the payment history](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/payments/check-the-payment-history.md): View billing payment history and download or print invoices for past payments.
- [Request a refund](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/payments/request-a-refund.md): Contact support to request a refund with a reason and affected server details, credited to the account balance on weekdays.
- [Contact our technical support](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/contact-our-technical-support.md): Contact Gcore technical support around the clock by live chat or by submitting a support ticket.
- [Manage hosting services via API](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/manage-hosting-services-via-api.md): Manage hosting services with Billmanager, DCImanager, and VMmanager for provisioning, payments, dedicated servers, virtual private servers.
- [Become a reseller and resell our services](https://docs.gcore.com/hosting/become-reseller-and-resell-our-services.md): Join the Gcore hosting reseller program to resell VPS or dedicated servers and receive a reseller discount after support approval.

# Gcore Colocation

> Gcore Colocation provides rack unit, full rack, and private cage options in data centers with power, cooling, network, and DDoS protection.

- [Colocation](https://docs.gcore.com/colocation/overview.md): Gcore Colocation provides rack unit, full rack, and private cage options in data centers with power, cooling, network, and DDoS protection.
- [Service requests](https://docs.gcore.com/colocation/service-requests.md): Colocation service requests cover data center access, parcel reception, equipment operations, dispatch, and Letters of Authorization.
- [Smart Hands](https://docs.gcore.com/colocation/smart-hands.md): Smart Hands provides Gcore engineers for physical data center tasks on colocated hardware, with priority tiers and time based billing.
- [Connectivity](https://docs.gcore.com/colocation/connectivity.md): Gcore colocation connectivity covers Direct Internet Access, cross-connects, and leased lines, with availability varying by location.

# Gcore Object Storage

> Gcore Object Storage offers S3 and SFTP buckets with access control, presigned URLs, lifecycle policies, and CDN delivery.

- [Object Storage](https://docs.gcore.com/storage.md): Gcore Object Storage offers S3 and SFTP buckets with access control, presigned URLs, lifecycle policies, and CDN delivery.
